package_info.why_malicious: The report does not analyze a specific software package or code artifact. Instead, it details a coordinated cybercriminal campaign targeting the Paris 2024 Olympics, involving the deployment of phishing kits, infostealer malware (such as Raccoon, Lumma, and Vidar), and typosquatting domains to steal credentials, payment information, and personal data. No individual package or codebase is examined in detail.

behavioral_signatures: Deployment of phishing kits that automate the creation and distribution of Olympic-themed phishing emails, payload delivery, and setup of phishing domains.
Use of infostealer malware (e.g., Raccoon, Lumma, Vidar) to access and exfiltrate browser-stored credentials, cryptocurrency wallets, and other sensitive user data.
Registration and operational use of typosquatting domains closely resembling official Olympic sites to lure victims.
Cloning of official Olympic ticketing and merchandise websites to harvest payment card information and personal details.
Utilization of bulk SMS and phone number spoofing services to distribute phishing links and lure event participants.
file_indicators: Website files and assets cloned from official Olympic ticketing or merchandise sites (e.g., HTML, CSS, JavaScript files with similar structure and content).
Phishing kit templates, configuration files, and automated email scripts referencing Olympic branding.
Infostealer malware binaries (e.g., Raccoon, Lumma, Vidar) delivered as attachments or downloads from phishing sites.
network_indicators: Connections to typosquatting domains mimicking Olympic-related sites (e.g., oympics[.]com, olmpics[.]com, olimpics[.]com).
Outbound traffic to known infostealer command-and-control (C2) infrastructure associated with Raccoon, Lumma, and Vidar.
Phishing email delivery infrastructure, including SMTP servers and webmail services used for mass campaigns.
Bulk SMS gateway endpoints and phone number spoofing services used to distribute phishing messages.
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor DNS and HTTP/S traffic for access to or communication with known typosquatting domains and cloned Olympic ticketing sites. Deploy endpoint detection to identify infostealer malware by monitoring for suspicious process behaviors, such as unauthorized access to browser credential stores and exfiltration of data over the network. Analyze inbound and outbound email traffic for mass-mailed Olympic-themed phishing messages, especially those originating from newly registered or suspicious domains. Monitor SMS and telephony logs for bulk messaging or spoofed numbers targeting event participants. Integrate threat intelligence feeds to block known malicious domains, C2 endpoints, and file hashes associated with infostealers and phishing operations.
